clue.text: After St Giles' day, many are turning rotten

blocks.note: St Giles' feast falls on 1 September, written SEPT I
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: Fruit picked after early September goes off on the tree.
explanation.walkthrough: St Giles' day is 1 September, so the date SEPT I is written out, and 'After' places the hundred behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Septic describes flesh infected and putrefying, so it works as a synonym for going bad or decayed.

clue.text: One works with a horse in film studio

indicators.note: in says the horse phrase sits inside the name of the studio

blocks.note: taken as written
gee, or gee-gee, is a childish word for a horse
Warner Bros is the Hollywood studio

explanation.surface: Someone employed on a film set to look after a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Warner Bros is the Hollywood studio, and the horse phrase lodges after its first letter. Gee-gee is nursery talk for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage-earner is anyone paid a regular wage for a job, a description of the person who works.

clue.text: Favourable maternity report for Mary's husband?

blocks.note: surface: a midwife's good news after a birth, that mother and child are fine
setter's reading: the third husband of Mary, Queen of Scots, an earl whose title splits into two words

explanation.walkthrough: After a birth the happy report is 'both well'; run together it is the Earl of BOTHWELL, who married Mary, Queen of Scots in 1567.
explanation.definitionFit: James Hepburn, Earl of Bothwell, was the third husband of the Scottish queen Mary Stuart.

clue.text: Lehar, wrongly assumed by many to be an Austrian composer

indicators.note: wrongly assumed means the letters are taken up in the wrong order

blocks.note: the operetta composer's name, used for its letters
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, standing for many

explanation.surface: A claim that Lehar is often wrongly thought to be Austrian, when he was Hungarian-born.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assumed by many' means the thousand is taken on board with the composer's letters before they are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Mahler was a Bohemian-born Austrian composer and conductor of the late Romantic era.

clue.text: Drawing of magic number in reverse

indicators.note: in reverse says the number is read from its last letter back
of here means made of, the number being part of what lies inside the outer word

blocks.note: taken as written
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A picture of a magic square, with its numbers running backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The turned number goes into the middle of MAGIC: MAG(NET)IC.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet draws iron towards it, so magnetic is the adjective for attracting or pulling.

clue.text: Hopper in convoluted dance

indicators.note: convoluted means twisted and tangled, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grasshopper caught up in some intricate dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornpipe is a lively solo dance traditionally associated with sailors.

clue.text: To snog in a boat is old-fashioned

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped anew, so the letters of the word before it are remade
in places the remade word inside the vessel

blocks.note: a canoe is a light boat
taken as written

explanation.surface: Kissing in a rowing boat is a quaint, dated sort of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' reads as one adjective, but splits into the word and its anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Canoodle is a jokey word for kissing and cuddling amorously, the same as snogging.

clue.text: One of twelve tribes, English and European

blocks.note: Dan was one of the twelve tribes of Israel
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Listing an ancient tribe alongside English and European peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: Danes come from Denmark, a Scandinavian country on the continent, so the nationality is one example of a European.

clue.text: A good teacher involves every one

indicators.note: involves means contains, so the answer is held within the words before it

blocks.note: the run of letters inside teacher

explanation.surface: A good teacher brings every pupil into the lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Each means every one taken individually, as in 'they paid a pound each'.

clue.text: Artist in crazy whirl

indicators.note: in puts the painter inside the word for crazy

blocks.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
gyte is a Scots word meaning mad or crazy

explanation.surface: A painter caught up in a mad spin.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for crazy is an obscure Scots one, and the Royal Academician is the usual crossword painter.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to spin or rotate rapidly, and whirl is a verb with the same meaning.

clue.text: Artificer mad about eastern church

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for mad surrounds the other letters

blocks.note: manic means frenzied or mad
E is the abbreviation for eastern
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A craftsman going wild around an Orthodox church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here means surrounding, so the word for mad wraps round the abbreviations rather than meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificer is a skilled craftsman, especially a military or naval mechanic who maintains equipment.

clue.text: Look forward to paying no tax, but have to cough up

blocks.note: to expect something is to look forward to it
O, the zero, stands for no or nothing
rates were a British local property tax

explanation.surface: Hoping to avoid tax but ending up having to pay after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cough up' looks like paying money; here it is literal coughing. Rates were the old British local tax on property.
explanation.definitionFit: To expectorate is to clear phlegm from the chest by coughing and spitting it out.

clue.text: Reference book where one turns up king in sex play

indicators.note: turns in a down clue means the next word is flipped to read upwards
in places the king's letter inside the word that follows

blocks.note: the Oxford English Dictionary
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
R, for rex, is the crossword king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry turning up a monarch in a racy drama.
explanation.walkthrough: OED + I + PU (up turned) + S(R)EX. Sophocles' tragedy, in which a king unknowingly marries his mother, fits 'sex play' slyly.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipus Rex is the Latin title of Sophocles' Greek tragedy Oedipus the King.

clue.text: Perverted one leering at ladies' underwear

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of its proper form, so the following letters are scrambled

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pervert ogling women's underwear in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' must become I, not ONE, for the letter count to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is the collective term for women's underclothes and nightwear.

clue.text: Say their trouble is neurotic

definitions.note: an adjective for the noun answer; the condition is the neurotic state

indicators.note: trouble means disturb or stir up, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone diagnosing a patient: whatever they claim is wrong is all in the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysteria is an old term for a neurotic disorder marked by uncontrolled emotional excess.

clue.text: Deceived by the devil, though not in so many words

blocks.note: an imp is a little devil
to lie is to deceive

explanation.surface: Being tricked by Satan through hints rather than outright statements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets the devil beside the deceiving: IMP then LIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implied is suggested indirectly rather than stated outright in explicit terms.

clue.text: Lame excuse I give for not voting?

blocks.clueFragment: excuse I give for not voting
blocks.note: an MP who is paired has agreed with an opponent that both will skip a vote, and says so in the first person

explanation.surface: A feeble reason someone offers for not turning up to vote.
explanation.walkthrough: The excuse is "I'm paired": in Parliament two opposing MPs can pair, so both stay away and the result is unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaired means weakened or damaged, as lame describes something disabled or not working properly.

clue.text: Nothing that the Pope wouldn't give Henry

definitions.text: that the Pope wouldn't give Henry

blocks.note: first meaning: a thing of no value or existence

blocks.clueFragment: that the Pope wouldn't give Henry
blocks.note: second meaning: Henry VIII sought from Rome a decree declaring his first marriage void

explanation.walkthrough: Pope Clement VII refused Henry VIII a decree that his marriage to Catherine of Aragon had never been valid, which led to the English break with Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A nullity is both a nonentity or nothing and a legal finding that a marriage was void.

clue.text: Influence of the Guardian - or what keeps it down

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: the clout a newspaper carries
second meaning: a heavy object placed on loose sheets so they do not blow away

explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian is the newspaper printing the puzzle, so its weight as a paper is the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A paperweight is a small heavy object holding loose sheets in place, punning on a newspaper's weight.

clue.text: English flower festival

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
the aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: An English flower show held as a seasonal celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival celebrating the resurrection of Jesus.

clue.text: Forward to Southend

blocks.note: read as South, abbreviated to its compass letter, followed by end

explanation.surface: Redirecting mail on to the seaside town of Southend.
explanation.walkthrough: Southend is an Essex seaside town; split it as South + end and shorten South to S.
explanation.definitionFit: To forward a letter is to send it on to another address.

clue.text: Space that is said to be less stuffy

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the answer is how the word is pronounced

blocks.note: airier means better ventilated, so less stuffy

explanation.surface: A room described as roomier and fresher.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is an expanse or region, a stretch of space.

clue.text: Realise modified model was the prototype

definitions.note: a phrase for being first, standing for the adjective

indicators.note: modified means altered, so the letters are changed into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: Finding that a reworked design was really the original version.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T Ford gives the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: The prototype is the first version made, so being the prototype means being the earliest one.

clue.text: A shark is certain to be found in the city

indicators.note: to be found in says one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword favourite
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A warning that predatory types are bound to lurk in the financial City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the city' looks like London's financial district, but it is the ancient Mesopotamian city that crosswords love.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan shark lends at extortionate interest, and a usurer is a lender charging exorbitant rates.

clue.text: Perishes, without help, from illness

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: to perish is to die
to abet is to help

explanation.surface: Someone dies of a disease for lack of medical help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but means outside: DI(ABET)ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabetes is a chronic disease in which the body cannot regulate blood sugar.

clue.text: Hollands in Switzerland

definitions.note: a place in Switzerland, standing for the city

blocks.note: first meaning: Hollands is Dutch gin
second meaning: a city found in Switzerland

explanation.walkthrough: Hollands looks like the Netherlands, but it is Dutch gin, whose old name comes from the juniper word, not the Swiss city.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva is both a Dutch juniper spirit and a major Swiss city on Lake Geneva.
